title: Conormal modules of presentations of S and of a principal localization of S agree up to free summands
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $g\in S$ and $S_g$ the localization of $S$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $n,m\ge0$, let $\alpha:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ and $\beta:R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to S_g$ be surjective homomorphisms of $R$-algebras from polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I=\ker\alpha$ and $J=\ker\beta$. Then $I/I^2$ is an $S$-module, $J/J^2$ is an $S_g$-module, and with $(I/I^2)_g$ the localization of the $S$-module $I/I^2$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] there is an isomorphism of $S_g$-modules $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^{\oplus n}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize, line 35776), whose proof uses Lemma 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), Lemma 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy) and Lemma 00S5 (lemma-conormal-module, line 35761)
